newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold stocks felt the brunt of a weak bullion price which on Monday sank to its lowest level in over three years.
Almost 2.5 percent was shaved off the value of the gold index, with dealers predicting further downside for the metal and shares on Tuesday.
"The run down in gold shares is purely on the gold price and it is expected to go even lower," one dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $359.25 an ounce in London morning trade on Monday, its lowest since October 7, 1993 as investors continued to cold-shoulder the metal in favour of booming equity markets.
Dealers said there was, however, no heavy sell-off of South African gold shares.
"There was very little trade...The market (in gold stocks) can best be described as lethargic, apathetic and with a distinct lack of interest," one dealer said.

Share weakness was also capped by the rand which spent most of the day holding weaker against the U.S. dollar above the 4.70 level. A softer rand/dollar exchange rate boosts the rand price of gold -- a boon for producers.

The gold index fell 2.48 percent or 36.2 points to 1,421.8 -- its lowest level in a year. Shares weighed down by bullion's fall included Freegold which ditched 130 cents or 3.88 percent to 32.20 rand, Dries which lost 165 cents to 45.85 rand and Vaal Reefs which dropped 600 cents to 286.50 rand.
"The weakness will carry on tomorrow (Tuesday) unless gold can bounce back above the $360 level, but this seems unlikely," a trader said.
Industrial shares ended a touch firmer retracing off firmer morning levels on futures-related basket trading and held steady for the afternoon in quiet dealings.
Stocks, initially rising on impetus from Wall Street's 101-point surge on Friday were seen eyeing the U.S. market for direction on Monday.
"If Wall Street is down tonight, it will not be conducive to us moving up tomorrow," a trader said.

The industrial index ended six points better at 7,882.5 after Malbak added 20 cents to 21 rand, Standard put on 30 cents to 183 rand but SAB and Amic each shed 50 cents to 115.75 rand and 165.25 rand respectively.
The overall index was off 21.3 points to 6,576.2.
March equity index futures contracts moved weaker as the trading session progressed after industrial and all-share instruments started the day on a firmer footing from Wall Street.
Gold contracts remained weak on the ailing bullion price.
The March all-share contract was at 6,065/73 from 6,095, the industrial index contract was at 7,650/65 from 7,640 and the gold index contract was at 980/97 from 1,018.
